sections.heading: Overview
content: Consistent with healthcare industry standards, Humana expects suppliers of durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies (DMEPOS) to retain proof of delivery (POD) documentation in their files and make it available to Humana upon request. Maintaining POD documentation is one of the supplier standards for DMEPOS suppliers participating in the Medicare Program as noted in the Code of Federal Regulations.

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires DMEPOS suppliers to maintain complete and accurate POD documentation, consistent with the standards of chapter 4, section 4.7.3.1 and chapter 5, section 5.10 of the Medicare Program Integrity Manual. Humana requires suppliers to make POD documentation available to Humana upon request. A Humana plan denies a charge for a service that lacks appropriate supplier POD documentation and requires reimbursement of any overpayment .

sections.heading: Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires in-network DMEPOS suppliers to maintain complete and accurate POD documentation, consistent with relevant state statutory and regulatory requirements. In the absence of relevant state statutory and regulatory requirements, Humana requires suppliers to maintain complete and accurate POD documentation, consistent with the standards of chapter 4, section 4.7.3.1 and chapter 5, section 5.10 of the Medicare Program Integrity Manual. Humana requires suppliers to make POD documentation available to Humana upon request. A Humana plan denies a charge for a service that lacks appropriate supplier POD documentation and requires reimbursement of any overpayment . Humana requires out-of-network DMEPOS suppliers to maintain complete and accurate POD documentation, consistent with relevant state statutory and regulatory requirements. Humana requires suppliers to make POD documentation available to Humana upon request. A Humana plan denies a charge for a service that lacks appropriate supplier POD documentation and requires reimbursement of any overpayment .

sections.heading: Definitions of Italicized Terms
content: • Durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies (DMEPOS) : All services included in Original Medicare’s DMEPOS Fee Schedule; all services included in Original Medicare’s Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition Items and Services (PEN) Fee Schedule; and all services that, though not included in those fee schedules, are of a kind that is typically included in those fee schedules. • Overpayment : An amount paid to the DMEPOS supplier for a service that lacks documentation.

sections.heading: General Humana Resources
content: • Availity – Providers can register for access to information on a variety of topics such as eligibility, benefits, referrals, authorizations, claims and electronic remittances. • Claims processing edit notifications – Alerts of upcoming claims payment changes are posted on the first Friday of each month. • Claims resources – Providers can find information on referrals, authorizations, electronic claim submissions and more. • Making it easier – This page contains an educational series for providers and healthcare professionals. • Medical and pharmacy coverage policies – Humana publishes determinations of coverage of medical procedures, devices and medications for the treatment of various conditions. There may be variances in coverage among plans. • Publications – This page can help you find our quarterly newsletter, provider manual and other resources to help you do business with us.
